Hi Eleanor — great to hear from you, and thanks for the options. A couple of quick notes before we lock:

1) EU bank holidays: Good Friday is on 29 Mar this year — some of our EU attendees may be OOO.
2) DST mismatch: US DST moved earlier this month; Europe shifts a week later, which often causes the one-hour offset between our US and EU participants — want to avoid a surprise.
3) APAC availability: Satoshi in Tokyo mentioned Golden Week in early May; he'd prefer earlier dates but will be OOO during Golden Week.

Given the overlap and the number of stakeholders, would Riverton consider a short-format split? Proposal: two focused 40-minute sessions on the same day so people can join the slot that best fits their local hours — one targeting EU/UK-friendly time, the other targeting APAC/India-friendly time. We can record and share notes.

If that sounds reasonable, Karthik and I can propose two time pairs that avoid EU Easter bank holiday and minimize DST confusion. I attached a quick timezone-summary and a suggested agenda (redwood-demo-agenda.pdf).

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

Thanks for the notes — happy to iterate on timing. Proposed approach (we'll handle invites/recording):

Option A (single day, two split sessions — preferred)
- Session 1 (EU/UK focus): Fri 29 Mar, 09:00–09:40 GMT (09:00 UTC) — short product walkthrough + Q&A for EU stakeholders
- Session 2 (APAC/India focus): Fri 29 Mar, 16:30–17:10 JST / 12:00–12:40 IST (07:30–08:10 UTC) — deep-dive on integration & latency knobs for APAC

Option B (if Friday is a problem for UK due to Good Friday)
- Move both split sessions to Mon 01 Apr, keeping the same local-friendly slots.

Rationale: keeping both sessions on the same day reduces context switching for our engineering leads and lets us record once. We avoid Mar 31 (EU DST shift) and also keep it before Golden Week.

Attachments: pre-demo-checklist.xlsx (request items for SSO, sample data, firewall/IPs)

If you confirm Option A, I'll send two calendar invites with separate Zoom links and a combined deck.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
